title: Unital natural tensor maps transport trivializations and cancel normalized comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with a chosen object $\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$, and let $\mathcal D$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Give $\mathcal D$ a symmetric braiding $\beta_{B,C}:B\otimes C\xrightarrow{\sim}C\otimes B$: natural braiding isomorphisms satisfying the two hexagon identities and $\beta_{C,B}\beta_{B,C}=1$. Write $\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$ for the unit of $\mathcal D$ and $\lambda,\rho$ for its left and right unitors; no monoidal structure on $\mathcal C$ is used. Let $P,G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be functors (preserving identities and compositions), let $u:P\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$ be an isomorphism, and put $W=G\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$. Suppose morphisms $\vartheta_K:PK\otimes W\to GK$, for every $K\in\mathcal C$, satisfy
$$G(v)\vartheta_K=\vartheta_L(Pv\otimes1_W)\quad(v:K\to L),\qquad\vartheta_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}}=\lambda_W(u\otimes1_W).$$
For any $T\in\mathcal C$, $V\in\mathcal D$ and isomorphism $c:V\xrightarrow{\sim}GT$, define
$$s=c^{-1}\vartheta_T\beta_{W,PT}:W\otimes PT\to V.$$
For every isomorphism $\eta:T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$, put
$$t=\rho_W(1_W\otimes(u\circ P\eta)):W\otimes PT\xrightarrow{\sim}W.$$
Then $s$ is invertible and
$$G(\eta)c\,s=t,\qquad t\,s^{-1}=G(\eta)c.$$

Independently, suppose a natural isomorphism $r:G\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ is given and put $\zeta=u\circ r_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}}:W\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$. Assume for every $K$ that
$$r_K\vartheta_K=\rho_{PK}(1_{PK}\otimes\zeta).$$
For arbitrary $T,V,c$ as above put $E=r_Tc:V\xrightarrow{\sim}PT$. Then
$$E s=\lambda_{PT}(\zeta\otimes1_{PT}),$$
and $s$ is invertible; this second assertion requires no $\eta$.

All the displayed equations, including the two equations defining each inverse, remain true after applying any functor out of $\mathcal D$. If supplied identifications carry the objects, tensor, unitors, symmetry, $P,G,u,\vartheta,c$ and any given $\eta,r$ to a second such datum, the resulting equations are its corresponding equations. No closed structure, exactness, adjunction or geometric realization is assumed.
